questions.q:
Toluene reacts with succinic anhydride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form compound P as the major product. P is subjected to Clemmensen reduction ($\text{Zn-Hg}$, conc. $\text{HCl}$) to yield Q. Finally, Q is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form the bicyclic compound R.

Identify the IUPAC names of the intermediate P and the final product R.
questions.question:
Toluene reacts with succinic anhydride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form compound P as the major product. P is subjected to Clemmensen reduction ($\text{Zn-Hg}$, conc. $\text{HCl}$) to yield Q. Finally, Q is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form the bicyclic compound R.

Identify the IUPAC names of the intermediate P and the final product R.
questions.solution:
Toluene undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation with succinic anhydride. The methyl group is an activating and ortho/para directing group. Due to steric hindrance, the para product predominates, forming 4-(4-methylphenyl)-4-oxobutanoic acid (P).

Clemmensen reduction ($\text{Zn-Hg}$, conc. $\text{HCl}$) selectively reduces the ketone carbonyl group to a methylene group without affecting the carboxylic acid, yielding 4-(4-methylphenyl)butanoic acid (Q).

Heating Q with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ causes an intramolecular Friedel-Crafts acylation. The electrophilic acylium ion attacks the ring at the position ortho to the alkyl chain (which is meta to the methyl group), forming a new six-membered ring. The resulting bicyclic compound R is 7-methyl-3,4-dihydronaphthalen-1(2H)-one.

Answer: P: 4-(4-methylphenyl)-4-oxobutanoic acid
R: 7-methyl-3,4-dihydronaphthalen-1(2H)-one

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Upon complete combustion of $1$ mole of an unknown hydrocarbon, the mass ratio of carbon dioxide to water produced is $44:9$. If $2.5$ moles of oxygen are consumed per mole of the hydrocarbon, what is its molecular formula?
questions.question: Upon complete combustion of $1$ mole of an unknown hydrocarbon, the mass ratio of carbon dioxide to water produced is $44:9$. If $2.5$ moles of oxygen are consumed per mole of the hydrocarbon, what is its molecular formula?
questions.solution:
Let the molecular formula of the hydrocarbon be $\text{C}_x\text{H}_y$. The general combustion equation is:

$\text{C}_x\text{H}_y + \left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right)\text{O}_2 \rightarrow x\text{CO}_2 + \dfrac{y}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The mass of $\text{CO}_2$ produced is $44x$ and the mass of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ produced is $18 \times \dfrac{y}{2} = 9y$.

Given the mass ratio of $\text{CO}_2$ to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is $44:9$, we have:

$\dfrac{44x}{9y} = \dfrac{44}{9}$

This simplifies to $\dfrac{x}{y} = 1$, which means $x = y$. The empirical formula is $\text{CH}$.

We are also given that $2.5$ moles of $\text{O}_2$ are consumed per mole of the hydrocarbon:

$x + \dfrac{y}{4} = 2.5$

Since $x = y$, substitute $y$ with $x$:

$x + \dfrac{x}{4} = 2.5$

$1.25x = 2.5 \Rightarrow x = 2$

Since $x = 2$ and $y = 2$, the molecular formula of the hydrocarbon is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$.

Answer: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An aromatic compound A ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$) is formed by passing alkyne B through a red-hot iron tube. Compound A on nitration yields a single mononitro derivative.
Alkyne B can be prepared by the reaction of a dihalide C with excess $\text{NaNH}_2$. Furthermore, B on hydration with dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{HgSO}_4$ gives compound D.

Identify the correct pair of compounds C and D.
questions.question:
An aromatic compound A ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$) is formed by passing alkyne B through a red-hot iron tube. Compound A on nitration yields a single mononitro derivative.
Alkyne B can be prepared by the reaction of a dihalide C with excess $\text{NaNH}_2$. Furthermore, B on hydration with dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{HgSO}_4$ gives compound D.

Identify the correct pair of compounds C and D.
options: C is 1,2-dichloropropane and D is propanal
C is 1,3-dichloropropane and D is propanone
C is 2,2-dichloropropane and D is propanone
C is 1,4-dichlorobutane and D is butanone
questions.solution:
The aromatic compound A ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$) is formed by the trimerization of alkyne B. This indicates that B is a 3-carbon alkyne, which is propyne ($\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$).
Trimerization of propyne in a red-hot iron tube yields 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene (mesitylene) as compound A. Mesitylene has all three of its ring hydrogen atoms in equivalent positions, so it yields a single mononitro derivative upon nitration, confirming our deduction.
Alkyne B (propyne) is prepared by the double dehydrohalogenation of a dihalide C using excess $\text{NaNH}_2$. Compound C must be a geminal or vicinal dihalide of propane, such as 2,2-dichloropropane or 1,2-dichloropropane. (1,3-dichloropropane would form cyclopropane instead).
Hydration of propyne (B) with dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{HgSO}_4$ follows Markovnikov's rule to give propan-2-one (propanone) as compound D.
Looking at the options, the correct pair is C = 2,2-dichloropropane and D = propanone.

Answer: C is 2,2-dichloropropane and D is propanone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the electrophilic aromatic nitration of $p$-methylacetanilide ($N$-(4-methylphenyl)acetamide). Identify the position of the incoming nitro group in the major product relative to the existing groups on the benzene ring.
questions.question: Consider the electrophilic aromatic nitration of $p$-methylacetanilide ($N$-(4-methylphenyl)acetamide). Identify the position of the incoming nitro group in the major product relative to the existing groups on the benzene ring.
options: Ortho to the methyl group and meta to the acetamido group
Ortho to both the acetamido and methyl groups
Meta to both the acetamido and methyl groups
Ortho to the acetamido group and meta to the methyl group
questions.solution:
In $p$-methylacetanilide, the benzene ring has two substituents: an acetamido group ($-\text{NHCOCH}_3$) and a methyl group ($-\text{CH}_3$) situated para to each other.

Both groups are ortho/para directing. However, the $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ group is a moderately strong activating group due to the lone pair on nitrogen, whereas the $-\text{CH}_3$ group is weakly activating via hyperconjugation.

When multiple directing groups are present, the more powerfully activating group dictates the position of the incoming electrophile. Thus, the $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ group controls the orientation.

Since the para position to the $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ group is already occupied by the $-\text{CH}_3$ group, the incoming nitro group will attach at the ortho position relative to the $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ group.

In a para-disubstituted benzene ring, a position that is ortho to one substituent is inherently meta to the other. Therefore, the nitro group will be ortho to the acetamido group and meta to the methyl group.

Answer: Ortho to the acetamido group and meta to the methyl group

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An acyclic alkene $X$ with molecular formula $C_7H_{14}$ yields acetone as one of its products upon reductive ozonolysis. When $X$ reacts with $HBr$ in the presence of peroxides, it forms a halogenated product $Y$ that exhibits exactly $4$ stereoisomers. The number of allylic hydrogen atoms ($\alpha$-hydrogens) in the major alkene $X$ is ________.
questions.question: An acyclic alkene $X$ with molecular formula $C_7H_{14}$ yields acetone as one of its products upon reductive ozonolysis. When $X$ reacts with $HBr$ in the presence of peroxides, it forms a halogenated product $Y$ that exhibits exactly $4$ stereoisomers. The number of allylic hydrogen atoms ($\alpha$-hydrogens) in the major alkene $X$ is ________.
questions.solution:
Acetone from the reductive ozonolysis of $X$ indicates the presence of a $(CH_3)_2C=$ group.

Given the molecular formula $C_7H_{14}$, the remaining fragment of the alkene must be $=CH-C_4H_9$. Thus, the structure of $X$ is $(CH_3)_2C=CH-C_4H_9$.

Reaction of $X$ with $HBr$ in the presence of peroxides proceeds via an anti-Markovnikov free radical addition. The bromine radical adds to the less substituted carbon (the $CH$ carbon) to generate the more stable tertiary radical, which then abstracts a hydrogen atom. The product $Y$ is $(CH_3)_2CH-CH(Br)-C_4H_9$.

For $Y$ to have exactly $4$ stereoisomers, it must possess $2$ chiral centers ($2^2 = 4$). The carbon bearing the bromine atom is one chiral center. The second chiral center must be located within the $-C_4H_9$ group. Among the isomeric butyl groups, only the sec-butyl group, $-CH(CH_3)(CH_2CH_3)$, provides a chiral center in this molecule.

Therefore, the alkene $X$ is $2,4$-dimethylhex-$2$-ene, with the structure $(CH_3)_2C=CH-CH(CH_3)(CH_2CH_3)$.

The $\alpha$-hydrogens (allylic hydrogens) in $X$ are those attached to the $sp^3$ carbons directly adjacent to the $C=C$ double bond. These are:
- Three hydrogens from the $C1$ methyl group.
- Three hydrogens from the methyl group attached to $C2$.
- One hydrogen from the $C4$ methine group.

Total number of $\alpha$-hydrogens = $3 + 3 + 1 = 7$.

Answer: $7$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 3-chloro-4-fluoronitrobenzene is treated with 1 equivalent of sodium methoxide in methanol, the major product formed is:
questions.question: When 3-chloro-4-fluoronitrobenzene is treated with 1 equivalent of sodium methoxide in methanol, the major product formed is:
questions.solution:
Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) requires a strong electron-withdrawing group (like -NO$_2$) at the ortho or para position relative to the leaving group to stabilize the carbanion intermediate.

In 3-chloro-4-fluoronitrobenzene, the fluorine atom is at the para position with respect to the -NO$_2$ group, while the chlorine atom is at the meta position. The -NO$_2$ group strongly activates the para position via both -M and -I effects, but only weakly activates the meta position via its -I effect.

Furthermore, in SNAr reactions, the rate-determining step is the initial nucleophilic attack on the aromatic ring. Fluorine, being more electronegative than chlorine, creates a larger partial positive charge on the attached carbon, making it more susceptible to nucleophilic attack. Thus, F is a better leaving group than Cl in SNAr reactions.

Therefore, the methoxide nucleophile will selectively attack the para position, displacing the fluorine atom to yield 3-chloro-4-methoxynitrobenzene as the major product.

Answer: 3-Chloro-4-methoxynitrobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown structural isomer 'X' of $C_5H_{12}$ is found to have the highest melting point among all its isomers. The number of structurally isomeric monochloro derivatives that 'X' can form upon photochemical chlorination, and its boiling point compared to n-pentane, respectively, are :
questions.question: An unknown structural isomer 'X' of $C_5H_{12}$ is found to have the highest melting point among all its isomers. The number of structurally isomeric monochloro derivatives that 'X' can form upon photochemical chlorination, and its boiling point compared to n-pentane, respectively, are :
questions.solution:
Among the structural isomers of $C_5H_{12}$, neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane) has the highest melting point due to its highly symmetrical spherical structure, which allows it to pack closely in the crystal lattice.

Therefore, isomer 'X' is neopentane.

Neopentane has 12 equivalent primary hydrogen atoms. Thus, it forms only 1 monochloro derivative upon photochemical chlorination.

The boiling point of alkanes decreases with an increase in branching due to a decrease in surface area and consequently weaker van der Waals forces. Hence, the boiling point of neopentane is lower than that of the straight-chain isomer, n-pentane.

Answer: 1 and lower

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When $5$-phenylpent-$1$-ene is heated in the presence of a catalytic amount of a strong acid, it undergoes an intramolecular reaction. The major organic product formed is:
questions.question: When $5$-phenylpent-$1$-ene is heated in the presence of a catalytic amount of a strong acid, it undergoes an intramolecular reaction. The major organic product formed is:
questions.solution:
Protonation of the terminal double bond of $5$-phenylpent-$1$-ene by the acid catalyst follows Markovnikov's rule, yielding a secondary carbocation at $\text{C}2$ of the pentyl chain.

The tethered benzene ring acts as an internal nucleophile, attacking this carbocation via an intramolecular electrophilic aromatic substitution (Friedel-Crafts alkylation).

The attack from the ortho position of the benzene ring onto the $\text{C}2$ carbocation forms a stable $6$-membered saturated ring fused to the benzene ring. The methyl group ($\text{C}1$ of the original chain) remains attached to the newly formed ring.

The resulting bicyclic product is $1$-methyl-$1,2,3,4$-tetrahydronaphthalene (also known as $1$-methyltetralin).

Answer: $1$-Methyl-$1,2,3,4$-tetrahydronaphthalene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following compounds, which one will undergo nucleophilic aromatic substitution at the fastest rate when treated with sodium methoxide?
questions.question: Among the following compounds, which one will undergo nucleophilic aromatic substitution at the fastest rate when treated with sodium methoxide?
questions.solution:
Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) proceeds via a carbanion intermediate (Meisenheimer complex). The rate of the reaction increases with the stability of this intermediate. Electron-withdrawing groups (EWGs) stabilize the carbanion, while electron-donating groups (ERGs) destabilize it.

The -CN group is a strong EWG. At the para position (in 4-chlorobenzonitrile), it stabilizes the intermediate through both strong -M (resonance) and -I (inductive) effects.

At the meta position (in 3-chlorobenzonitrile), the -CN group can only exert its -I effect, which provides less stabilization than the combined -M and -I effects at the para position.

The -OCH$_3$ group (in 4-chloroanisole) is an ERG due to its strong +M effect, which strongly deactivates the ring towards SNAr.

The -CH$_3$ group (in 4-chlorotoluene) is an ERG due to its +I and hyperconjugation effects, which also deactivates the ring.

Therefore, 4-chlorobenzonitrile will undergo the reaction at the fastest rate.

Answer: 4-Chlorobenzonitrile

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following two reaction sequences starting from toluene:

Sequence 1: Toluene $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{KMnO_4, \ H^+, \ \Delta}}$ P $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl, \ AlCl_3}}$ Q

Sequence 2: Toluene $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl, \ AlCl_3}}$ R (major) $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{KMnO_4, \ H^+, \ \Delta}}$ S

Identify the final products Q and S. (Note: If a reagent fails to react, the starting material of that step is recovered as the product).
questions.question:
Consider the following two reaction sequences starting from toluene:

Sequence 1: Toluene $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{KMnO_4, \ H^+, \ \Delta}}$ P $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl, \ AlCl_3}}$ Q

Sequence 2: Toluene $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl, \ AlCl_3}}$ R (major) $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{KMnO_4, \ H^+, \ \Delta}}$ S

Identify the final products Q and S. (Note: If a reagent fails to react, the starting material of that step is recovered as the product).
options: Q is Benzoic acid; S is Benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid
Q is 3-Ethylbenzoic acid; S is 4-Ethylbenzoic acid
Q is 3-Ethylbenzoic acid; S is Benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid
Q is Benzoic acid; S is 4-Ethylbenzoic acid
questions.solution:
In Sequence 1, toluene is subjected to vigorous oxidation with $\mathrm{KMnO_4}/\mathrm{H^+}$ and heat. The side-chain methyl group is oxidized to a carboxylic acid group, yielding benzoic acid as product P. Benzoic acid contains the strongly deactivating $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group, which reduces the electron density on the benzene ring significantly. As a result, it does not undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation when treated with $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl}$ and $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$. Thus, no reaction occurs in the second step, and Q remains benzoic acid.

In Sequence 2, toluene first undergoes Friedel-Crafts alkylation with $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl}$ and $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$. The methyl group is ortho/para-directing. Due to steric hindrance at the ortho position, the major product R is 1-ethyl-4-methylbenzene (p-ethyltoluene). When R is treated with $\mathrm{KMnO_4}/\mathrm{H^+}$ and heat, any alkyl side chain with at least one benzylic hydrogen is oxidized entirely to a $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group. Both the methyl and ethyl groups are oxidized, yielding benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (terephthalic acid) as product S.

Answer: Q is Benzoic acid; S is Benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound containing carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen has a vapour density of $44$. Complete combustion of $0.88\text{ g}$ of this compound produces $1.76\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ and $0.72\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The number of oxygen atoms present in one molecule of the compound is ________.
questions.question: An organic compound containing carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen has a vapour density of $44$. Complete combustion of $0.88\text{ g}$ of this compound produces $1.76\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ and $0.72\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The number of oxygen atoms present in one molecule of the compound is ________.
questions.solution:
Molar mass of the compound $= 2 \times \text{Vapour density} = 2 \times 44 = 88\text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Moles of the compound burnt $= \dfrac{0.88}{88} = 0.01\text{ mol}$

Moles of $\text{CO}_2$ produced $= \dfrac{1.76}{44} = 0.04\text{ mol}$
Moles of carbon in $0.01\text{ mol}$ of compound $= 0.04\text{ mol}$
Number of carbon atoms per molecule $= \dfrac{0.04}{0.01} = 4$

Moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ produced $= \dfrac{0.72}{18} = 0.04\text{ mol}$
Moles of hydrogen in $0.01\text{ mol}$ of compound $= 2 \times 0.04 = 0.08\text{ mol}$
Number of hydrogen atoms per molecule $= \dfrac{0.08}{0.01} = 8$

Let the molecular formula be $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_x$.
Molar mass $= (4 \times 12) + (8 \times 1) + (x \times 16) = 88$
$48 + 8 + 16x = 88$
$56 + 16x = 88$
$16x = 32 \implies x = 2$

Thus, there are $2$ oxygen atoms in one molecule of the compound.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hepta-1,6-dien-3-one is reacted with excess $\text{HBr}$ to form an intermediate compound $\text{A}$. Compound $\text{A}$ is then treated with 1 equivalent of $\text{NaI}$ in acetone to yield the major product $\text{B}$. The structure of product $\text{B}$ is:
questions.question: Hepta-1,6-dien-3-one is reacted with excess $\text{HBr}$ to form an intermediate compound $\text{A}$. Compound $\text{A}$ is then treated with 1 equivalent of $\text{NaI}$ in acetone to yield the major product $\text{B}$. The structure of product $\text{B}$ is:
questions.solution:
The reactant hepta-1,6-dien-3-one ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$) has two double bonds: an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone (C1=C2) and an isolated terminal alkene (C6=C7).

Addition of excess $\text{HBr}$.
For the conjugated alkene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-$), electrophilic addition places the proton at the $\alpha$-carbon to avoid placing a positive charge adjacent to the electron-withdrawing carbonyl group. The bromide ion attacks the $\beta$-carbon, yielding a primary bromide: $\text{BrCH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-$.
For the isolated alkene ($-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$), addition follows Markovnikov's rule, yielding a secondary bromide: $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$.
Thus, intermediate $\text{A}$ is 1,6-dibromoheptan-3-one: $\text{BrCH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$.

Finkelstein reaction with 1 equivalent of $\text{NaI}$ in acetone.
This reaction proceeds via an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism. The primary bromide at C1 is significantly less sterically hindered and more reactive towards nucleophilic substitution than the secondary bromide at C6. Therefore, the iodide ion selectively displaces the primary bromide.

The major product $\text{B}$ is 6-bromo-1-iodoheptan-3-one: $\text{ICH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$.

Answer: $\text{ICH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Benzene reacts with a cyclic anhydride X in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form a keto-acid Y. Compound Y undergoes Clemmensen reduction to form Z. Heating Z with polyphosphoric acid yields benzosuberone (6,7,8,9-tetrahydro-5H-benzo[a]cyclohepten-5-one), which contains a seven-membered cyclic ketone fused to the benzene ring.

Identify the starting cyclic anhydride X.
questions.question:
Benzene reacts with a cyclic anhydride X in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form a keto-acid Y. Compound Y undergoes Clemmensen reduction to form Z. Heating Z with polyphosphoric acid yields benzosuberone (6,7,8,9-tetrahydro-5H-benzo[a]cyclohepten-5-one), which contains a seven-membered cyclic ketone fused to the benzene ring.

Identify the starting cyclic anhydride X.
questions.solution:
The final product, benzosuberone, consists of a benzene ring fused to a seven-membered cyclic ketone. The seven-membered ring shares two carbon atoms with the benzene ring, meaning the side chain that cyclizes must contain five carbon atoms.

Working backwards (retrosynthetically):
The intramolecular acylation of Z to form a seven-membered ring requires Z to be 5-phenylpentanoic acid.
Z is formed by the Clemmensen reduction of the keto-acid Y. Therefore, Y must be 5-oxo-5-phenylpentanoic acid.
Y is produced by the Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with the cyclic anhydride X. To yield a five-carbon keto-acid, the anhydride X must be a saturated five-carbon cyclic anhydride.
Thus, X is glutaric anhydride (pentanedioic anhydride).

Answer: Glutaric anhydride

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following sequence of reagents is most suitable for the conversion of 1-propyne into trans-2-hexene?
questions.question: Which of the following sequence of reagents is most suitable for the conversion of 1-propyne into trans-2-hexene?
questions.solution:
1-propyne reacts with the strong base $\text{NaNH}_2$ to deprotonate the terminal alkyne, forming the propynide ion.

The propynide ion undergoes an $S_N2$ reaction with n-propyl bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$) to form a 6-carbon internal alkyne, 2-hexyne. Using isopropyl bromide would lead to a branched alkyne or elimination.

To obtain trans-2-hexene, the internal alkyne (2-hexyne) must be reduced using Birch reduction ($\text{Na}$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$). Lindlar catalyst would yield the cis-alkene, and $\text{H}_2/\text{Pd-C}$ would over-reduce it to hexane.

Answer: (i) $\text{NaNH}_2$, (ii) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$, (iii) $\text{Na}$ / liq. $\text{NH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
1,2-dibromo-3,3-dimethylcyclohexane $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) Zn, }\Delta}$ Intermediate $\xrightarrow{\text{(ii) HCl}}$ Major Product (P)

The major product (P) is:
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
1,2-dibromo-3,3-dimethylcyclohexane $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) Zn, }\Delta}$ Intermediate $\xrightarrow{\text{(ii) HCl}}$ Major Product (P)

The major product (P) is:
questions.solution:
Treatment of 1,2-dibromo-3,3-dimethylcyclohexane with Zn dust and heat causes dehalogenation, yielding 3,3-dimethylcyclohexene.

Addition of HCl begins with the protonation of the alkene. Protonation at C1 generates a secondary carbocation at C2, which is adjacent to the quaternary C3 carbon.

To achieve greater stability, a 1,2-methyl shift occurs from C3 to C2, transforming the secondary carbocation into a more stable tertiary carbocation at C3.

Finally, the chloride ion attacks this tertiary carbocation, resulting in the formation of 1-chloro-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane as the major product.

Answer: 1-chloro-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct sequence of reagents for the conversion of n-hexane to a mixture of benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate is:
questions.question: The correct sequence of reagents for the conversion of n-hexane to a mixture of benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate is:
options: (i) $V_2O_5, 773\text{ K}, 10-20\text{ atm}$; (ii) $CO, HCl, \text{anhyd. } AlCl_3, CuCl$; (iii) Conc. $NaOH$
(i) $Mo_2O_3, 773\text{ K}, 10-20\text{ atm}$; (ii) $CO, HCl, \text{anhyd. } AlCl_3, CuCl$; (iii) Dil. $NaOH$
questions.solution:
The starting material is n-hexane. Aromatization of n-hexane over $V_2O_5$ at $773\text{ K}$ and $10-20\text{ atm}$ yields benzene.

Benzene lacks a methyl group, so it cannot undergo the Etard reaction. To introduce an aldehyde group, the Gattermann-Koch reaction is used. Treatment with $CO$ and $HCl$ in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_3$ and $CuCl$ converts benzene to benzaldehyde.

Benzaldehyde lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens. Upon treatment with concentrated $NaOH$, it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction (disproportionation) to yield benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate.

Thus, the correct sequence is aromatization, followed by Gattermann-Koch formylation, and finally the Cannizzaro reaction.

Answer: (i) $V_2O_5, 773\text{ K}, 10-20\text{ atm}$; (ii) $CO, HCl, \text{anhyd. } AlCl_3, CuCl$; (iii) Conc. $NaOH$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A cyclic alkene 'X' undergoes reductive ozonolysis to yield a single compound 'Y' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$. Compound 'Y' gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent and a yellow precipitate when treated with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$. When the same alkene 'X' is subjected to vigorous oxidation with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$, it yields compound 'Z'. Which of the following statements is correct regarding compound 'Z'?
questions.question: A cyclic alkene 'X' undergoes reductive ozonolysis to yield a single compound 'Y' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$. Compound 'Y' gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent and a yellow precipitate when treated with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$. When the same alkene 'X' is subjected to vigorous oxidation with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$, it yields compound 'Z'. Which of the following statements is correct regarding compound 'Z'?
options: It forms a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent and gives effervescence with aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$.
It gives a yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ but does not react with aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$.
It does not give a yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ but gives effervescence with aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$.
It gives a yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ and gives effervescence with aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$.
questions.solution:
Compound 'Y' ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$) is formed by the reductive ozonolysis of a cyclic alkene, so it must be a dicarbonyl compound.

Since 'Y' gives a positive Tollens' test, it contains an aldehyde group. It also gives a positive iodoform test (yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$), indicating the presence of a methyl ketone group ($-\text{COCH}_3$).

With 7 carbon atoms in total, 'Y' must be 6-oxoheptanal: $\text{CH}_3\text{CO(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{CHO}$.

The cyclic alkene 'X' that yields 'Y' upon ozonolysis is 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene.

Vigorous oxidation of 'X' with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ cleaves the double bond. The substituted carbon becomes a ketone, and the unsubstituted carbon is oxidized fully to a carboxylic acid. Thus, compound 'Z' is 6-oxoheptanoic acid: $\text{CH}_3\text{CO(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{COOH}$.

Compound 'Z' contains a methyl ketone group, so it will give a yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$. It also contains a carboxylic acid group, so it will give effervescence with aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$. It lacks an aldehyde group, so it will not respond to Tollens' reagent.

Answer: It gives a yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ and gives effervescence with aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$.

questions.q:
When 2-bromo-3-methylbutane is heated with alcoholic KOH, it gives a major product A. Product A is then subjected to ozonolysis with $\text{O}_3$ followed by boiling $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

The final organic products formed are:
questions.question:
When 2-bromo-3-methylbutane is heated with alcoholic KOH, it gives a major product A. Product A is then subjected to ozonolysis with $\text{O}_3$ followed by boiling $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

The final organic products formed are:
questions.solution:
The starting material is 2-bromo-3-methylbutane: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$.

Heating with alcoholic KOH causes dehydrohalogenation (an elimination reaction). According to Zaitsev's rule, the more substituted alkene is formed as the major product.
Elimination of HBr yields 2-methylbut-2-ene as the major product A:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$

Product A is then reacted with $\text{O}_3$ followed by boiling $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The absence of a reducing agent (like Zn or dimethyl sulfide) means this is an oxidative ozonolysis.

During oxidative ozonolysis, the carbon-carbon double bond is cleaved.
The disubstituted carbon atom, $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=$, becomes a ketone: propan-2-one (acetone).
The monosubstituted carbon atom, $=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$, initially forms an aldehyde (ethanal) which is further oxidized to a carboxylic acid: ethanoic acid (acetic acid).

Therefore, the final organic products are propan-2-one and ethanoic acid.

Answer: Propan-2-one and ethanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Monobromination of an isomer of cresol (methylphenol) in $\text{CS}_2$ yields a major product in which the newly introduced bromine atom is situated at a meta position with respect to the methyl group. Which isomer(s) of cresol exhibit this behavior?
questions.question: Monobromination of an isomer of cresol (methylphenol) in $\text{CS}_2$ yields a major product in which the newly introduced bromine atom is situated at a meta position with respect to the methyl group. Which isomer(s) of cresol exhibit this behavior?
questions.solution:
To determine which isomer(s) of cresol yield a product where the incoming bromine is meta to the methyl group, we evaluate the directing effects in each isomer. The $-\text{OH}$ group is a much stronger activating group than the $-\text{CH}_3$ group, so $-\text{OH}$ dictates the position of electrophilic attack.

For $o$-cresol (2-methylphenol): The $-\text{OH}$ group is at position 1 and $-\text{CH}_3$ is at position 2. Bromination occurs primarily at the para position with respect to $-\text{OH}$ (position 4) due to less steric hindrance. Position 4 is meta to the $-\text{CH}_3$ group at position 2.

For $p$-cresol (4-methylphenol): The $-\text{OH}$ group is at position 1 and $-\text{CH}_3$ is at position 4. The para position is blocked. Bromination occurs at the ortho position with respect to $-\text{OH}$ (position 2). Position 2 is meta to the $-\text{CH}_3$ group at position 4.

For $m$-cresol (3-methylphenol): The $-\text{OH}$ group is at position 1 and $-\text{CH}_3$ is at position 3. Bromination occurs para to $-\text{OH}$ (position 4, which is ortho to $-\text{CH}_3$) or ortho to $-\text{OH}$ (position 6, which is para to $-\text{CH}_3$). Neither major product has the bromine meta to the methyl group.

Thus, both $o$-cresol and $p$-cresol yield a major product where the bromine is meta to the methyl group.

Answer: Both $o$-cresol and $p$-cresol

questions.q:
An unknown hydrocarbon 'P' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$ is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:
(i) $\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{FeCl}_3 \rightarrow \text{Q}$ (major product)
(ii) $\text{Br}_2$, $h\nu$ (1 equivalent) $\rightarrow \text{R}$
(iii) alc. $\text{KOH}$, $\Delta \rightarrow 1\text{-chloro-4-(prop-1-en-2-yl)benzene}$

The structure of the starting hydrocarbon 'P' is:
questions.question:
An unknown hydrocarbon 'P' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$ is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:
(i) $\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{FeCl}_3 \rightarrow \text{Q}$ (major product)
(ii) $\text{Br}_2$, $h\nu$ (1 equivalent) $\rightarrow \text{R}$
(iii) alc. $\text{KOH}$, $\Delta \rightarrow 1\text{-chloro-4-(prop-1-en-2-yl)benzene}$

The structure of the starting hydrocarbon 'P' is:
questions.solution:
The final product is 1-chloro-4-(prop-1-en-2-yl)benzene. The presence of a branched prop-1-en-2-yl side chain indicates that the elimination in step (iii) occurred from a 2-halopropan-2-yl group.

Working backwards:
Step (iii): Dehydrohalogenation of 'R' with alc. KOH yields the alkene. Thus, 'R' must be 1-chloro-4-(2-bromopropan-2-yl)benzene.
Step (ii): 'R' is formed by benzylic bromination of 'Q'. This implies 'Q' has an isopropyl group, making it 1-chloro-4-isopropylbenzene.
Step (i): 'Q' is formed by the electrophilic aromatic chlorination of 'P'. Since 'Q' is a para-substituted chlorobenzene with an isopropyl group, the starting hydrocarbon 'P' must be isopropylbenzene (cumene).

If 'P' were n-propylbenzene, the sequence would yield 1-chloro-4-(prop-1-enyl)benzene instead.

Answer: Isopropylbenzene

questions.q: Hex-$3$-yne is subjected to reduction using sodium in liquid ammonia to yield product $\text{X}$. In a separate reaction, hex-$3$-yne is reduced using hydrogen gas in the presence of Lindlar's catalyst to yield product $\text{Y}$. Both $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ are then independently treated with $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CCl}_4$. Identify the stereochemical nature of the final dibrominated products obtained from $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ respectively.
questions.question: Hex-$3$-yne is subjected to reduction using sodium in liquid ammonia to yield product $\text{X}$. In a separate reaction, hex-$3$-yne is reduced using hydrogen gas in the presence of Lindlar's catalyst to yield product $\text{Y}$. Both $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ are then independently treated with $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CCl}_4$. Identify the stereochemical nature of the final dibrominated products obtained from $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ respectively.
options: $\text{X}$ yields a racemic mixture, $\text{Y}$ yields a meso compound
$\text{X}$ yields a meso compound, $\text{Y}$ yields a racemic mixture
questions.solution:
Reduction of hex-$3$-yne with $\text{Na}$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ (Birch reduction) yields trans-hex-$3$-ene ($\text{X}$).

Reduction of hex-$3$-yne with $\text{H}_2$ in the presence of Lindlar's catalyst yields cis-hex-$3$-ene ($\text{Y}$).

The addition of $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CCl}_4$ to an alkene proceeds via an anti-addition mechanism.

Anti-addition of bromine to a trans-alkene (like trans-hex-$3$-ene) results in a meso compound.

Anti-addition of bromine to a cis-alkene (like cis-hex-$3$-ene) results in a racemic mixture of enantiomers.

Therefore, $\text{X}$ yields a meso compound and $\text{Y}$ yields a racemic mixture.

Answer: $\text{X}$ yields a meso compound, $\text{Y}$ yields a racemic mixture

questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
n-propylbenzene $\xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4}$ P (major) $\xrightarrow{\text{NBS}/\Delta}$ Q (major) $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}/\Delta}$ R (major)

The IUPAC name of the final major product R is:
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
n-propylbenzene $\xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4}$ P (major) $\xrightarrow{\text{NBS}/\Delta}$ Q (major) $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}/\Delta}$ R (major)

The IUPAC name of the final major product R is:
questions.solution:
Nitration of n-propylbenzene with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ yields 1-propyl-4-nitrobenzene (P) as the major product due to the ortho/para directing nature of the alkyl group and steric hindrance at the ortho position.

Reaction of P with NBS (N-bromosuccinimide) and heat results in free radical substitution at the benzylic position, giving 1-(1-bromopropyl)-4-nitrobenzene (Q).

Treatment of Q with alcoholic KOH and heat causes dehydrohalogenation (E2 elimination). According to Zaitsev's rule, the more substituted and conjugated alkene is formed as the major product, yielding 1-(4-nitrophenyl)prop-1-ene (R).

Answer: 1-(4-nitrophenyl)prop-1-ene

questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:

Anisole $\xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{Cl, anhydrous AlCl}_3}$ Major product A $\xrightarrow{\text{conc. HNO}_3, \text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4}$ Major product B

The IUPAC name of the major product B is:
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence:

Anisole $\xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{Cl, anhydrous AlCl}_3}$ Major product A $\xrightarrow{\text{conc. HNO}_3, \text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4}$ Major product B

The IUPAC name of the major product B is:
questions.solution:
Friedel-Crafts alkylation of anisole with $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ yields 4-methylanisole as the major product A, because the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group is an ortho/para director and the para position is sterically less hindered.

Nitration of 4-methylanisole involves a competition between two activating groups: the strongly activating $-\text{OCH}_3$ group and the weakly activating $-\text{CH}_3$ group. The stronger activating group ($-\text{OCH}_3$) dictates the orientation of the incoming electrophile ($\text{NO}_2^+$).

Since the para position with respect to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group is already occupied by the methyl group, the nitration occurs at the ortho position relative to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group. Thus, the major product B is 4-methyl-2-nitroanisole.

Answer: 4-Methyl-2-nitroanisole

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $2$-Methylpentan-$3$-ol is heated with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ to yield a major alkene $B$. Alkene $B$ is then treated with $HBr$ in the presence of peroxide to form product $C$. The total number of possible stereoisomers for product $C$ is ________.
questions.question: $2$-Methylpentan-$3$-ol is heated with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ to yield a major alkene $B$. Alkene $B$ is then treated with $HBr$ in the presence of peroxide to form product $C$. The total number of possible stereoisomers for product $C$ is ________.
questions.solution:
Protonation of $2$-methylpentan-$3$-ol followed by the loss of a water molecule forms a secondary carbocation at $C3$: $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH^{+}-CH_2-CH_3$.

A $1,2$-hydride shift occurs from $C2$ to $C3$ to form a more stable tertiary carbocation: $CH_3-C^{+}(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$.

Elimination of a proton from the adjacent carbon yields the more substituted, major Saytzeff alkene $B$, which is $2$-methylpent-$2$-ene: $CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_2-CH_3$.

Reaction of alkene $B$ with $HBr$ in the presence of peroxide follows anti-Markovnikov regioselectivity. The bromine radical adds to the less substituted carbon of the double bond ($C3$) to form a more stable tertiary radical at $C2$, which then abstracts a hydrogen atom. The resulting product $C$ is $3$-bromo-$2$-methylpentane: $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH(Br)-CH_2-CH_3$.

In product $C$, $C3$ is a chiral center because it is attached to four different groups: a hydrogen atom, a bromine atom, an ethyl group, and an isopropyl group. $C2$ is not a chiral center because it is attached to two identical methyl groups.

Since there is exactly $1$ chiral center, the total number of stereoisomers for product $C$ is $2^1 = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct sequence of reagents to synthesize 2-chloro-4-nitrobenzoic acid from toluene as the major product.
questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of reagents to synthesize 2-chloro-4-nitrobenzoic acid from toluene as the major product.
questions.solution:
To synthesize 2-chloro-4-nitrobenzoic acid from toluene, the order of electrophilic aromatic substitution and oxidation reactions is critical because the directing nature of the substituent changes upon oxidation (from ortho/para-directing $-\text{CH}_3$ to meta-directing $-\text{COOH}$).

Nitration of toluene with $\text{conc. HNO}_3$ and $\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4$ yields 4-nitrotoluene as the major isomer due to steric hindrance at the ortho position.

Chlorination of 4-nitrotoluene with $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{FeCl}_3$ takes advantage of the synergistic directing effects of the two groups. The $-\text{CH}_3$ group is ortho/para directing (para is blocked), and the $-\text{NO}_2$ group is meta directing. Both direct the incoming electrophile ($\text{Cl}^+$) to the position ortho to the methyl group, yielding 2-chloro-4-nitrotoluene.

Oxidation of the methyl group in 2-chloro-4-nitrotoluene using acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ with heat converts it to a carboxylic acid group, producing the target molecule, 2-chloro-4-nitrobenzoic acid.

If oxidation were performed earlier, the resulting $-\text{COOH}$ group would direct subsequent electrophiles to the meta position, leading to incorrect substitution patterns.

Answer: (i) $\text{conc. HNO}_3, \text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4$ (ii) $\text{Cl}_2, \text{FeCl}_3$ (iii) $\text{KMnO}_4, \text{H}^+, \Delta$

questions.q:
An unknown alkyne $\text{A}$ having the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}$ reacts with $\text{H}_2$ in the presence of Lindlar's catalyst to give an alkene $\text{B}$. Reductive ozonolysis of $\text{B}$ (using $\text{O}_3$ followed by $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) yields only propanal. When the same alkyne $\text{A}$ is treated with sodium in liquid ammonia, it gives an alkene $\text{C}$.

Identify the correct statement comparing the physical properties of isomers $\text{B}$ and $\text{C}$.
questions.question:
An unknown alkyne $\text{A}$ having the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}$ reacts with $\text{H}_2$ in the presence of Lindlar's catalyst to give an alkene $\text{B}$. Reductive ozonolysis of $\text{B}$ (using $\text{O}_3$ followed by $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) yields only propanal. When the same alkyne $\text{A}$ is treated with sodium in liquid ammonia, it gives an alkene $\text{C}$.

Identify the correct statement comparing the physical properties of isomers $\text{B}$ and $\text{C}$.
options: $\text{B}$ has zero dipole moment and a higher melting point than $\text{C}$
$\text{B}$ has a non-zero dipole moment and a higher melting point than $\text{C}$
$\text{C}$ has zero dipole moment and a higher melting point than $\text{B}$
$\text{C}$ has a higher dipole moment and a lower melting point than $\text{B}$
questions.solution:
Reductive ozonolysis of $\text{B}$ yields only propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$). This indicates that $\text{B}$ is a symmetrical alkene, specifically hex-$3$-ene. Thus, the starting alkyne $\text{A}$ is hex-$3$-yne.

Reaction of hex-$3$-yne with $\text{H}_2$ and Lindlar's catalyst yields the cis-isomer. Therefore, $\text{B}$ is cis-hex-$3$-ene.

Reaction of hex-$3$-yne with $\text{Na}$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ yields the trans-isomer. Therefore, $\text{C}$ is trans-hex-$3$-ene.

The trans-isomer ($\text{C}$) is symmetrical and its individual bond dipoles cancel out, resulting in a zero dipole moment. In contrast, the cis-isomer ($\text{B}$) has a non-zero dipole moment.

Furthermore, the trans-isomer ($\text{C}$) has a more symmetrical structure, which allows it to pack more efficiently in the crystal lattice compared to the cis-isomer. As a result, $\text{C}$ has a higher melting point than $\text{B}$.

Therefore, $\text{C}$ has zero dipole moment and a higher melting point than $\text{B}$.

Answer: $\text{C}$ has zero dipole moment and a higher melting point than $\text{B}$
