questions.q:
Two reaction sequences are proposed to synthesize $p$-bromostyrene from ethylbenzene.

Sequence A: (i) $\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3$ (ii) $\text{Cl}_2/h\nu$ (iii) alc. KOH, $\Delta$
Sequence B: (i) $\text{Cl}_2/h\nu$ (ii) alc. KOH, $\Delta$ (iii) $\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3$

Given below are two statements regarding these sequences:
Statement I: Sequence B is an incorrect route because the final bromination step ($\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3$) will primarily result in electrophilic addition to the vinyl group rather than substitution on the benzene ring.
Statement II: Sequence A is the correct route because the ethyl group is ortho/para directing and unreactive towards electrophilic addition, allowing selective ring bromination first.

Choose the most appropriate option:
questions.question:
Two reaction sequences are proposed to synthesize $p$-bromostyrene from ethylbenzene.

Sequence A: (i) $\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3$ (ii) $\text{Cl}_2/h\nu$ (iii) alc. KOH, $\Delta$
Sequence B: (i) $\text{Cl}_2/h\nu$ (ii) alc. KOH, $\Delta$ (iii) $\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3$

Given below are two statements regarding these sequences:
Statement I: Sequence B is an incorrect route because the final bromination step ($\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3$) will primarily result in electrophilic addition to the vinyl group rather than substitution on the benzene ring.
Statement II: Sequence A is the correct route because the ethyl group is ortho/para directing and unreactive towards electrophilic addition, allowing selective ring bromination first.

Choose the most appropriate option:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.solution:
In Sequence B, the first two steps convert the ethyl group into a vinyl group, forming styrene. When styrene is subjected to $\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3$, the highly reactive carbon-carbon double bond undergoes rapid electrophilic addition of bromine, which outcompetes the desired electrophilic aromatic substitution on the ring. Thus, Sequence B fails to produce $p$-bromostyrene.

In Sequence A, the aromatic ring is brominated first. The ethyl group is an activating, ortho/para directing group that does not react with $\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3$ via addition, allowing selective formation of $p$-bromoethylbenzene. Subsequent benzylic halogenation and elimination successfully yield $p$-bromostyrene. Therefore, both statements are correct.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following nitrogen-containing compounds:
(A) Quinoline
(B) 1,2,3,4-Tetrahydroisoquinoline
(C) 3,4-Dihydroquinolin-2(1H)-one
(D) 1,2,3,4-Tetrahydroquinoline

The correct increasing order of their reactivity towards aromatic electrophilic substitution is:
questions.question:
Consider the following nitrogen-containing compounds:
(A) Quinoline
(B) 1,2,3,4-Tetrahydroisoquinoline
(C) 3,4-Dihydroquinolin-2(1H)-one
(D) 1,2,3,4-Tetrahydroquinoline

The correct increasing order of their reactivity towards aromatic electrophilic substitution is:
questions.solution:
The rate of electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS) depends on the electron density of the aromatic ring. Electron-donating groups increase the rate, while electron-withdrawing groups decrease it.

In (A) Quinoline, the benzene ring is fused to an electron-deficient pyridine ring, which strongly deactivates it via $-I$ and $-R$ effects.

In (B) 1,2,3,4-Tetrahydroisoquinoline, the nitrogen atom is not directly attached to the benzene ring. The benzene ring is only attached to alkyl carbons, experiencing weak $+I$ and $+H$ activating effects.

In (C) 3,4-Dihydroquinolin-2(1H)-one, the nitrogen atom is directly attached to the benzene ring, but it is part of an amide group. Its lone pair is delocalized into the adjacent carbonyl group, reducing its $+R$ effect on the benzene ring. Thus, it is moderately activating.

In (D) 1,2,3,4-Tetrahydroquinoline, the nitrogen atom is directly attached to the benzene ring as a secondary amine. Its lone pair is fully available for delocalization into the benzene ring, exerting a strong $+R$ effect and making it highly activated.

Therefore, the increasing order of electron density and EAS reactivity is A $<$ B $<$ C $<$ D.

Answer: A $<$ B $<$ C $<$ D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When benzene is heated with $3,3$-dimethylbut-$1$-ene in the presence of $\text{HF}$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.question: When benzene is heated with $3,3$-dimethylbut-$1$-ene in the presence of $\text{HF}$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.solution:
Protonation of the double bond in $3,3$-dimethylbut-$1$-ene by $\text{HF}$ follows Markovnikov's rule, initially forming a secondary carbocation ($3,3$-dimethylbutan-$2$-yl cation).

This secondary carbocation is adjacent to a quaternary carbon, so it undergoes a rapid $1,2$-methyl shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation ($2,3$-dimethylbutan-$2$-yl cation).

Benzene then acts as a nucleophile and undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with this rearranged tertiary carbocation.

The final major product is $2,3$-dimethyl-$2$-phenylbutane.

Answer: $2,3$-Dimethyl-$2$-phenylbutane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A cyclic hydrocarbon 'M' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}$ yields $5$-oxohexanal on reductive ozonolysis. When 'M' is treated with $\text{HBr}$ in the presence of benzoyl peroxide, it forms a major product 'P'. The IUPAC name of 'P' is :
questions.question: A cyclic hydrocarbon 'M' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}$ yields $5$-oxohexanal on reductive ozonolysis. When 'M' is treated with $\text{HBr}$ in the presence of benzoyl peroxide, it forms a major product 'P'. The IUPAC name of 'P' is :
questions.solution:
The reductive ozonolysis of 'M' ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}$) yields $5$-oxohexanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$).

To deduce the structure of 'M', we connect the carbonyl carbons (C$1$ of the aldehyde and C$5$ of the ketone) with a double bond. This intramolecular ring closure results in a five-membered ring with a methyl group attached to one of the double-bonded carbons. Thus, 'M' is $1$-methylcyclopentene.

When $1$-methylcyclopentene is treated with $\text{HBr}$ in the presence of benzoyl peroxide, it undergoes anti-Markovnikov addition (peroxide effect). The bromine free radical adds to the less substituted carbon of the double bond (C$2$) to generate a more stable tertiary free radical at C$1$. Subsequent abstraction of a hydrogen atom yields $1$-bromo-$2$-methylcyclopentane as the major product 'P'.

Answer: $1$-bromo-$2$-methylcyclopentane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the major product formed when $N$-allylbut-2-enamide is treated with 2 equivalents of $\text{HBr}$?
questions.question: What is the major product formed when $N$-allylbut-2-enamide is treated with 2 equivalents of $\text{HBr}$?
questions.solution:
The reactant $N$-allylbut-2-enamide has the structure $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$. It contains two different carbon-carbon double bonds: an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated amide and an isolated terminal alkene.

For the $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated system ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-$), the electron-withdrawing nature of the carbonyl group destabilizes any positive charge at the $\alpha$-position. Therefore, protonation occurs at the $\alpha$-carbon to form a more stable carbocation at the $\beta$-position (which is also stabilized by resonance in the enol form). Nucleophilic attack by $\text{Br}^-$ then occurs at the $\beta$-carbon, resulting in anti-Markovnikov-type addition with respect to the carbonyl group. This yields the fragment $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-$.

For the isolated terminal alkene ($-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$), electrophilic addition follows Markovnikov's rule. Protonation occurs at the terminal carbon to form the more stable secondary carbocation, followed by $\text{Br}^-$ attack at the internal carbon. This yields the fragment $-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$.

Combining these two fragments gives the major product: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An unknown alkene on ozonolysis with $\text{O}_3$ followed by treatment with $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ yields propan-2-one and butanoic acid as the only organic products.

The IUPAC name of the starting alkene is:
questions.question:
An unknown alkene on ozonolysis with $\text{O}_3$ followed by treatment with $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ yields propan-2-one and butanoic acid as the only organic products.

The IUPAC name of the starting alkene is:
questions.solution:
The reaction conditions ($\text{O}_3$ followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) correspond to oxidative ozonolysis.

Under these conditions, a disubstituted alkene carbon yields a ketone, while a monosubstituted alkene carbon yields a carboxylic acid.

The products are propan-2-one (a ketone) and butanoic acid (a carboxylic acid).
Propan-2-one is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_3$, which indicates that one side of the original double bond was a disubstituted carbon with two methyl groups: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=$.

Butanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. In oxidative ozonolysis, a carboxylic acid is formed from a monosubstituted alkene carbon. Thus, the other side of the double bond was $=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

Joining the two fragments gives the structure of the alkene:
$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$

Numbering the longest carbon chain to give the double bond the lowest possible number, we start from the left:
1: $\text{CH}_3$
2: $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)$
3: $\text{CH}$
4: $\text{CH}_2$
5: $\text{CH}_2$
6: $\text{CH}_3$

The IUPAC name is 2-methylhex-2-ene.

Answer: 2-methylhex-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Complete reductive ozonolysis of $960 \text{ mg}$ of a hydrocarbon C yields solely $2,6$-heptanedione as the product. The volume of $\text{H}_2$ gas (in $\text{mL}$) that would be consumed by $960 \text{ mg}$ of C during complete catalytic hydrogenation at STP ($1 \text{ atm}, 273 \text{ K}$) is
questions.question: Complete reductive ozonolysis of $960 \text{ mg}$ of a hydrocarbon C yields solely $2,6$-heptanedione as the product. The volume of $\text{H}_2$ gas (in $\text{mL}$) that would be consumed by $960 \text{ mg}$ of C during complete catalytic hydrogenation at STP ($1 \text{ atm}, 273 \text{ K}$) is
questions.solution:
Since the ozonolysis of hydrocarbon C yields a single product containing two carbonyl groups, C must be a monocycloalkene.

The product is $2,6$-heptanedione: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C(=O)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C(=O)}-\text{CH}_3$.

To find the structure of C, we connect the two carbonyl carbons (C2 and C6) to form a double bond. This creates a five-membered ring with methyl groups on the two carbons of the double bond.
Thus, hydrocarbon C is $1,2$-dimethylcyclopentene.

The molecular formula of $1,2$-dimethylcyclopentene is $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}$.
Molar mass of C $= 7 \times 12 + 12 = 96 \text{ g/mol}$.

Moles of C present $= \dfrac{960 \times 10^{-3} \text{ g}}{96 \text{ g/mol}} = 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Since C has one double bond, $1$ mole of C consumes $1$ mole of $\text{H}_2$ gas during complete catalytic hydrogenation.
Moles of $\text{H}_2$ consumed $= 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Volume of $\text{H}_2$ gas at STP ($1 \text{ atm}, 273 \text{ K}$) $= 0.01 \text{ mol} \times 22400 \text{ mL/mol} = 224 \text{ mL}$.

Answer: $224$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A hydrocarbon 'Y' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{12}$ absorbs two moles of $\text{H}_2$ on catalytic hydrogenation. On reductive ozonolysis, one mole of 'Y' yields one mole of hexane-$2,5$-dione and one mole of ethanedial. The hydrocarbon 'Y' is :
questions.question: A hydrocarbon 'Y' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{12}$ absorbs two moles of $\text{H}_2$ on catalytic hydrogenation. On reductive ozonolysis, one mole of 'Y' yields one mole of hexane-$2,5$-dione and one mole of ethanedial. The hydrocarbon 'Y' is :
questions.solution:
Degree of unsaturation (DBE) for $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{12} = 8 + 1 - \dfrac{12}{2} = 3$.

Since one mole of 'Y' absorbs two moles of $\text{H}_2$, it contains two double bonds. The remaining $1$ DBE indicates the presence of one ring.

Reductive ozonolysis of 'Y' yields hexane-$2,5$-dione ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$) and ethanedial ($\text{OHC}-\text{CHO}$).

To find the structure of 'Y', we perform a retrosynthetic analysis by removing the oxygen atoms from the carbonyl groups of the products and connecting the respective carbon atoms with double bonds.

Aligning the two fragments:
The two aldehyde carbons of ethanedial connect to the two ketone carbons of hexane-$2,5$-dione. This forms a six-membered ring with methyl groups at the $1$ and $4$ positions, and double bonds at the $1,3$ positions.

Thus, the structure of 'Y' is $1,4$-dimethylcyclohexa-$1,3$-diene.

Answer: $1,4$-dimethylcyclohexa-$1,3$-diene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
(1,2-dibromoethyl)cyclopentane $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) Zn, }\Delta}$ Intermediate $\xrightarrow{\text{(ii) HCl}}$ Major Product (P)

The major product (P) is:
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
(1,2-dibromoethyl)cyclopentane $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) Zn, }\Delta}$ Intermediate $\xrightarrow{\text{(ii) HCl}}$ Major Product (P)

The major product (P) is:
questions.solution:
Reaction of (1,2-dibromoethyl)cyclopentane with Zn and heat leads to dehalogenation, forming vinylcyclopentane.

Upon addition of HCl, the terminal double bond is protonated to form a secondary carbocation at the carbon adjacent to the five-membered ring, yielding a 1-cyclopentylethyl cation.

To relieve angle strain, the five-membered ring undergoes expansion. One of the ring C-C bonds migrates to the exocyclic carbocation, expanding the ring to a six-membered cyclohexane ring and leaving a secondary carbocation on the adjacent ring carbon.

This new secondary carbocation is adjacent to a tertiary carbon (which bears a methyl group). A 1,2-hydride shift occurs to move the positive charge to this tertiary carbon, forming a highly stable tertiary carbocation.

Nucleophilic attack by the chloride ion on the tertiary carbocation yields 1-chloro-1-methylcyclohexane as the major product.

Answer: 1-chloro-1-methylcyclohexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Complete reductive ozonolysis of an acyclic hydrocarbon B yields acetone, glyoxal, and acetaldehyde in a $1:1:1$ molar ratio. It is observed that $19.2 \text{ mg}$ of B consumes $8.96 \text{ mL}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas measured at STP ($1 \text{ atm}$ and $273 \text{ K}$). The number of allylic hydrogen atoms present in the hydrocarbon B is
questions.question: Complete reductive ozonolysis of an acyclic hydrocarbon B yields acetone, glyoxal, and acetaldehyde in a $1:1:1$ molar ratio. It is observed that $19.2 \text{ mg}$ of B consumes $8.96 \text{ mL}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas measured at STP ($1 \text{ atm}$ and $273 \text{ K}$). The number of allylic hydrogen atoms present in the hydrocarbon B is
questions.solution:
From the ozonolysis products, we can reconstruct the carbon skeleton of the acyclic hydrocarbon B.

The products are:
Acetone: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O}$ (a terminal fragment)
Glyoxal: $\text{O=CH}-\text{CH=O}$ (a middle fragment)
Acetaldehyde: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH=O}$ (a terminal fragment)

Connecting the carbonyl carbons by removing oxygen atoms to form double bonds gives the structure of B:
$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}-\text{CH=CH}-\text{CH}_3$
This is $2$-methylhexa-$2,4$-diene.

Let us verify with the hydrogenation data:
Molecular formula of B is $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}$, so its molar mass is $7 \times 12 + 12 = 96 \text{ g/mol}$.
Moles of B $= \dfrac{19.2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ g}}{96 \text{ g/mol}} = 2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$.
Moles of $\text{H}_2$ consumed $= \dfrac{8.96 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L}}{22.4 \text{ L/mol}} = 4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$.
The ratio of $\text{H}_2$ to B is $2:1$, which confirms the presence of $2$ double bonds.

Now, we count the allylic hydrogen atoms (hydrogens attached to $\text{sp}^3$ carbons that are directly bonded to $\text{sp}^2$ carbons of the diene system):
In $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}-\text{CH=CH}-\text{CH}_3$, the allylic groups are:
1. The two methyl groups attached to the first double bond: $3 + 3 = 6$ hydrogens.
2. The terminal methyl group attached to the second double bond: $3$ hydrogens.

Total number of allylic hydrogens $= 6 + 3 = 9$.

Answer: $9$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An alkene 'P' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}$ undergoes reductive ozonolysis to yield two different carbonyl compounds: a ketone 'Q' and a straight-chain aldehyde 'R'. When 'P' is treated with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$, it yields the same ketone 'Q' along with a carboxylic acid 'S'. If 'Q' and 'S' contain an equal number of carbon atoms, the IUPAC name of alkene 'P' is
questions.question: An alkene 'P' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}$ undergoes reductive ozonolysis to yield two different carbonyl compounds: a ketone 'Q' and a straight-chain aldehyde 'R'. When 'P' is treated with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$, it yields the same ketone 'Q' along with a carboxylic acid 'S'. If 'Q' and 'S' contain an equal number of carbon atoms, the IUPAC name of alkene 'P' is
questions.solution:
Given that alkene 'P' ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}$) undergoes reductive ozonolysis to give a ketone 'Q' and a straight-chain aldehyde 'R', 'P' must be a trisubstituted alkene.

Upon vigorous oxidation with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$, the aldehyde part is oxidized to a carboxylic acid 'S', while the ketone 'Q' remains unchanged.

Since 'P' has 8 carbon atoms and 'Q' and 'S' have an equal number of carbon atoms, both 'Q' and 'S' must have 4 carbon atoms each.

The 4-carbon ketone 'Q' is butan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$).

The 4-carbon carboxylic acid 'S' is butanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$), which means the straight-chain aldehyde 'R' is butanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$).

Reconstructing the alkene 'P' by joining the carbonyl carbons of butan-2-one and butanal gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

The IUPAC name of this alkene is 3-methylhept-3-ene.

Answer: 3-methylhept-3-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reactions to form products P, Q, R, and S:
I. Benzene + $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}\xrightarrow{\text{Anhydrous AlCl}_3}$ P
II. Toluene + $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}\xrightarrow{\text{Anhydrous AlCl}_3}$ Q (major product)
III. Phenol + $(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}\xrightarrow{\text{Pyridine}}$ R
IV. Aniline + $(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}\xrightarrow{\text{Pyridine}}$ S

The correct increasing order of reactivity of the products P, Q, R, and S towards aromatic electrophilic substitution is:
questions.question:
Consider the following reactions to form products P, Q, R, and S:
I. Benzene + $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}\xrightarrow{\text{Anhydrous AlCl}_3}$ P
II. Toluene + $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}\xrightarrow{\text{Anhydrous AlCl}_3}$ Q (major product)
III. Phenol + $(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}\xrightarrow{\text{Pyridine}}$ R
IV. Aniline + $(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}\xrightarrow{\text{Pyridine}}$ S

The correct increasing order of reactivity of the products P, Q, R, and S towards aromatic electrophilic substitution is:
questions.solution:
First, identify the products of the given reactions:
Reaction I produces P (Acetophenone). The $-\text{COCH}_3$ group is strongly deactivating due to $-R$ and $-I$ effects.
Reaction II produces Q (4-Methylacetophenone). It contains a deactivating $-\text{COCH}_3$ group and an activating $-\text{CH}_3$ group ($+I, +H$). The presence of the methyl group makes Q less deactivated than P.
Reaction III produces R (Phenyl acetate). The $-\text{OCOCH}_3$ group is activating due to its $+R$ effect.
Reaction IV produces S (Acetanilide). The $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ group is also activating due to its $+R$ effect.

Comparing the activating groups in R and S: Nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen, so the lone pair on nitrogen is more readily available for delocalization into the benzene ring than the lone pair on oxygen. Therefore, $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ is a stronger activating group than $-\text{OCOCH}_3$, making S more reactive than R.

Comparing the deactivated rings P and Q: Q has an electron-donating methyl group which partially offsets the deactivating effect of the acetyl group, making Q more reactive than P.

Overall, the increasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic aromatic substitution is P $<$ Q $<$ R $<$ S.

Answer: P $<$ Q $<$ R $<$ S

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Toluene is treated with oleum to form a major product P. Compound P is heated with molten sodium hydroxide followed by acidification to yield compound Q. Finally, Q is distilled with zinc dust to produce compound R. Identify the structures of compounds Q and R respectively.
questions.question: Toluene is treated with oleum to form a major product P. Compound P is heated with molten sodium hydroxide followed by acidification to yield compound Q. Finally, Q is distilled with zinc dust to produce compound R. Identify the structures of compounds Q and R respectively.
questions.solution:
Toluene undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with oleum. The methyl group is an ortho/para directing group. Due to steric hindrance at the ortho position, the major product P is $p$-toluenesulfonic acid.

Fusion of $p$-toluenesulfonic acid with molten NaOH followed by acidification replaces the sulfonate group ($-\text{SO}_3\text{H}$) with a hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$), yielding $p$-cresol (compound Q).

Distillation of $p$-cresol with zinc dust reduces the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group, regenerating the aromatic hydrocarbon. The methyl group remains unaffected on the ring, so compound R is toluene.

Answer: $p$-cresol and toluene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the molecule 4-methoxy-4'-nitrobiphenyl. Four positions on the aromatic rings are labeled as follows:
Position $a$: ortho to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group
Position $b$: meta to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group
Position $c$: ortho to the $-\text{NO}_2$ group
Position $d$: meta to the $-\text{NO}_2$ group

During an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction, the incoming electrophile will predominantly attack at:
questions.question:
Consider the molecule 4-methoxy-4'-nitrobiphenyl. Four positions on the aromatic rings are labeled as follows:
Position $a$: ortho to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group
Position $b$: meta to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group
Position $c$: ortho to the $-\text{NO}_2$ group
Position $d$: meta to the $-\text{NO}_2$ group

During an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction, the incoming electrophile will predominantly attack at:
questions.solution:
The molecule 4-methoxy-4'-nitrobiphenyl consists of two phenyl rings connected to each other. One ring has an electron-donating $-\text{OCH}_3$ group, and the other has an electron-withdrawing $-\text{NO}_2$ group.

The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group activates its attached ring towards electrophilic attack via a strong $+M$ effect. Conversely, the $-\text{NO}_2$ group strongly deactivates its attached ring via a $-M$ effect. Therefore, electrophilic attack will occur preferentially on the more electron-rich ring, which is the one bearing the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group.

The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group is an ortho/para directing group. Since the para position of this ring is already occupied by the other phenyl ring (the 4'-nitrophenyl group), the incoming electrophile must attach at the ortho position relative to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group.

This corresponds to Position $a$.

Answer: Position $a$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:

n-heptane $\xrightarrow{Cr_2O_3, 773\text{ K}, 10-20\text{ atm}} A \xrightarrow{CrO_3, (CH_3CO)_2O, 273-283\text{ K}} B \xrightarrow{H_3O^+, \Delta} C \xrightarrow{\text{Conc. } NaOH} D + E$

The intermediates $B$ and $C$ are respectively:
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence:

n-heptane $\xrightarrow{Cr_2O_3, 773\text{ K}, 10-20\text{ atm}} A \xrightarrow{CrO_3, (CH_3CO)_2O, 273-283\text{ K}} B \xrightarrow{H_3O^+, \Delta} C \xrightarrow{\text{Conc. } NaOH} D + E$

The intermediates $B$ and $C$ are respectively:
options: $B$ is Benzoic anhydride, $C$ is Benzoic acid
$B$ is Benzylidene diacetate, $C$ is Benzyl alcohol
questions.solution:
The aromatization of n-heptane over $Cr_2O_3$ at $773\text{ K}$ and high pressure yields toluene ($A$).

Toluene is oxidized by chromic oxide ($CrO_3$) in the presence of acetic anhydride. The reaction stops at the aldehyde stage because the intermediate formed is a gem-diacetate, specifically benzylidene diacetate ($B$), which is stable under the reaction conditions and prevents further oxidation to benzoic acid.

Upon acid hydrolysis ($H_3O^+, \Delta$), the benzylidene diacetate ($B$) is converted to benzaldehyde ($C$).

Benzaldehyde then undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated $NaOH$ to form sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol ($D$ and $E$).

Answer: $B$ is Benzylidene diacetate, $C$ is Benzaldehyde

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When $3.0\text{ g}$ of an organic compound with a molar mass of $150\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ is completely burnt in excess oxygen, $5.28\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ is produced. The number of carbon atoms present in one molecule of the compound is ________.
questions.question: When $3.0\text{ g}$ of an organic compound with a molar mass of $150\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ is completely burnt in excess oxygen, $5.28\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ is produced. The number of carbon atoms present in one molecule of the compound is ________.
questions.solution:
Moles of the organic compound $= \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Molar mass}} = \dfrac{3.0}{150} = 0.02\text{ mol}$

Moles of $\text{CO}_2$ produced $= \dfrac{5.28}{44} = 0.12\text{ mol}$

Applying the Principle of Atomic Conservation (POAC) on carbon, all the carbon from the compound is converted into $\text{CO}_2$.
Therefore, moles of carbon in the sample $= 0.12\text{ mol}$

Number of moles of carbon per mole of the compound $= \dfrac{0.12}{0.02} = 6$

Thus, there are $6$ carbon atoms in one molecule of the compound.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Toluene is subjected to Birch reduction using sodium in liquid ammonia and ethanol to yield a major product $P$. Product $P$ is then treated with ozone followed by zinc dust and water to yield two organic products $Q$ and $R$. The IUPAC names of $Q$ and $R$ are:
questions.question: Toluene is subjected to Birch reduction using sodium in liquid ammonia and ethanol to yield a major product $P$. Product $P$ is then treated with ozone followed by zinc dust and water to yield two organic products $Q$ and $R$. The IUPAC names of $Q$ and $R$ are:
questions.solution:
The methyl group in toluene is an electron-donating group (EDG). During Birch reduction, EDGs direct the reduction such that the carbon atom bearing the substituent remains $sp^2$ hybridized.

Thus, the Birch reduction of toluene yields 1-methylcyclohexa-1,4-diene as the major product $P$. The double bonds in $P$ are located at the C1-C2 and C4-C5 positions.

Next, $P$ undergoes reductive ozonolysis ($\text{O}_3$ followed by $\text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}$). This cleaves the two double bonds:

1. Cleavage of the C4=C5 and C1=C2 bonds breaks the ring into two fragments.
2. The C2-C3-C4 fragment forms propanedial ($\text{OHC}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$).
3. The C5-C6-C1 fragment forms 3-oxobutanal ($\text{OHC}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$), since C1 has the methyl group attached.

Therefore, the products $Q$ and $R$ are propanedial and 3-oxobutanal.

Answer: Propanedial and 3-oxobutanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The complete combustion of $1$ mole of an acyclic hydrocarbon belonging to the homologous series with the general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$ requires exactly $4.5$ moles of oxygen. The molecular formula of the hydrocarbon is:
questions.question: The complete combustion of $1$ mole of an acyclic hydrocarbon belonging to the homologous series with the general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$ requires exactly $4.5$ moles of oxygen. The molecular formula of the hydrocarbon is:
questions.solution:
The general equation for the combustion of an alkene ($\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$) is:

$\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n} + \dfrac{3n}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow n\text{CO}_2 + n\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Given that $1$ mole of the hydrocarbon requires $4.5$ moles of $\text{O}_2$, we can equate the stoichiometric coefficient of oxygen to $4.5$:

$\dfrac{3n}{2} = 4.5$

$3n = 9 \Rightarrow n = 3$

Substituting $n = 3$ into the general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$, we get $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$.

Answer: $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following sets of aromatic compounds completely fails to undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation?
questions.question: Which of the following sets of aromatic compounds completely fails to undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation?
questions.solution:
Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation reactions do not occur on strongly deactivated benzene rings. Groups like $-\mathrm{NO_2}$, $-\mathrm{COOH}$, $-\mathrm{CHO}$, $-\mathrm{CN}$, and $-\mathrm{COR}$ are strong electron-withdrawing groups that decrease the electron density on the benzene ring to such an extent that the electrophile cannot attack it.

Furthermore, aniline has an $-\mathrm{NH_2}$ group which acts as a Lewis base. It reacts with the Lewis acid catalyst (like $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$) to form a strongly deactivated complex, thus preventing the Friedel-Crafts reaction.

Chlorobenzene, toluene, and anisole have groups that do not deactivate the ring strongly enough to prevent the reaction (halogens are weakly deactivating, while alkyl and alkoxy groups are activating).

Therefore, the set containing aniline, nitrobenzene, and benzoic acid completely fails to undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation.

Answer: Aniline, nitrobenzene, benzoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown hydrocarbon $X$ ($C_6H_{10}$) undergoes reductive ozonolysis to yield a single product $Y$. When $Y$ is treated with excess iodine and aqueous $NaOH$, it produces a yellow precipitate of iodoform along with the disodium salt of succinic acid. The IUPAC name of hydrocarbon $X$ is
questions.question: An unknown hydrocarbon $X$ ($C_6H_{10}$) undergoes reductive ozonolysis to yield a single product $Y$. When $Y$ is treated with excess iodine and aqueous $NaOH$, it produces a yellow precipitate of iodoform along with the disodium salt of succinic acid. The IUPAC name of hydrocarbon $X$ is
questions.solution:
The formation of iodoform ($CHI_3$) upon treatment with $I_2/NaOH$ indicates that the product $Y$ contains at least one methyl ketone group ($-COCH_3$).

The formation of the disodium salt of succinic acid ($NaOOC-CH_2-CH_2-COONa$) along with iodoform from a single molecule $Y$ implies that $Y$ is a diketone that undergoes a double haloform reaction.

Working backwards, the structure of $Y$ must be hexane-2,5-dione ($CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH_2-CO-CH_3$).

Since $Y$ is the sole product of the reductive ozonolysis of $X$ ($C_6H_{10}$), $X$ must be a cyclic alkene that cleaves to form hexane-2,5-dione. Joining the carbonyl carbons of $Y$ to form a double bond gives a four-membered ring with two methyl groups on the double bond.

Thus, the structure of $X$ is 1,2-dimethylcyclobutene.

Answer: 1,2-dimethylcyclobutene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following sequence of reactions starting from benzene:
Benzene $\xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl, AlCl}_3}$ P (major) $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2\text{, Fe}}$ Q (major) $\xrightarrow{\text{NBS, } h\nu}$ R $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH, }\Delta}$ S (major)

The IUPAC name of the final major product 'S' is:
questions.question:
Consider the following sequence of reactions starting from benzene:
Benzene $\xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl, AlCl}_3}$ P (major) $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2\text{, Fe}}$ Q (major) $\xrightarrow{\text{NBS, } h\nu}$ R $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH, }\Delta}$ S (major)

The IUPAC name of the final major product 'S' is:
questions.solution:
Reaction of benzene with n-propyl chloride and $\text{AlCl}_3$ generates a primary carbocation ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2^+$), which undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to form a more stable secondary carbocation ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}^+\text{CH}_3$). Electrophilic aromatic substitution yields isopropylbenzene (cumene) as the major product 'P'.

Bromination of isopropylbenzene with $\text{Br}_2/\text{Fe}$ occurs via electrophilic aromatic substitution. The bulky isopropyl group directs the incoming bromine predominantly to the para position due to steric hindrance, yielding 1-bromo-4-isopropylbenzene as 'Q'.

Reaction with NBS and light causes free radical bromination selectively at the benzylic position. The tertiary benzylic hydrogen is replaced to form 1-bromo-4-(2-bromopropan-2-yl)benzene as 'R'.

Heating 'R' with alcoholic KOH causes E2 elimination (dehydrohalogenation) of the side-chain bromine, forming a double bond conjugated with the benzene ring. The final product 'S' is 1-bromo-4-(prop-1-en-2-yl)benzene.

Answer: 1-bromo-4-(prop-1-en-2-yl)benzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following functional groups when attached to a benzene ring:
$-\text{NO}_2$, $-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{OH}$, $-\text{CN}$, $-\text{Br}$, $-\text{OCH}_3$, $-\text{CF}_3$, $-\text{F}$, $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$, $-\text{CHO}$

The number of groups that are deactivating towards electrophilic aromatic substitution but direct the incoming electrophile to ortho and para positions is
questions.question:
Consider the following functional groups when attached to a benzene ring:
$-\text{NO}_2$, $-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{OH}$, $-\text{CN}$, $-\text{Br}$, $-\text{OCH}_3$, $-\text{CF}_3$, $-\text{F}$, $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$, $-\text{CHO}$

The number of groups that are deactivating towards electrophilic aromatic substitution but direct the incoming electrophile to ortho and para positions is
questions.solution:
In electrophilic aromatic substitution, activating groups are generally ortho/para directing, while deactivating groups are generally meta directing.

However, halogens are a notable exception. They are deactivating overall because their strong inductive electron withdrawal ($-I$ effect) makes the ring less reactive than benzene. At the same time, they are ortho/para directing because their resonance effect ($+R$ effect) via lone pair donation stabilizes the carbocation intermediate when the electrophile attacks at the ortho or para positions.

From the given list, the halogens are $-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{Br}$, and $-\text{F}$.

Let us classify the other groups:
$\bullet-\text{NO}_2$, $-\text{CN}$, $-\text{CF}_3$, $-\text{CHO}$ are deactivating and meta directing.
$\bullet-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{OH}$, $-\text{OCH}_3$, $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ are activating and ortho/para directing.

Therefore, there are exactly 3 groups ($-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{Br}$, $-\text{F}$) that are both deactivating and ortho/para directing.

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Complete combustion of $0.50 \text{ g}$ of an oxygen-containing organic compound gave $0.88 \text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ and $0.90 \text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The percentage of oxygen in the compound is _______.

[Given : Molar mass (in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$) $\text{C}: 12, \text{H}: 1, \text{O}: 16$]
questions.question:
Complete combustion of $0.50 \text{ g}$ of an oxygen-containing organic compound gave $0.88 \text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ and $0.90 \text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The percentage of oxygen in the compound is _______.

[Given : Molar mass (in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$) $\text{C}: 12, \text{H}: 1, \text{O}: 16$]
questions.solution:
Mass of carbon in the compound $= \dfrac{12}{44} \times \text{Mass of CO}_2 = \dfrac{12}{44} \times 0.88 = 0.24 \text{ g}$

Mass of hydrogen in the compound $= \dfrac{2}{18} \times \text{Mass of H}_2\text{O} = \dfrac{2}{18} \times 0.90 = 0.10 \text{ g}$

Total mass of carbon and hydrogen $= 0.24 + 0.10 = 0.34 \text{ g}$

Since the compound contains only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen, the mass of oxygen is:
Mass of oxygen $= \text{Total mass of compound} - (\text{Mass of C} + \text{Mass of H}) = 0.50 - 0.34 = 0.16 \text{ g}$

Percentage of oxygen $= \dfrac{0.16}{0.50} \times 100 = 32\%$

Answer: $32$

Consider the following aromatic compounds:
Chlorobenzene, Anisole, Toluene, Nitrobenzene, Acetophenone, Phenol, Benzoic acid.

The number of compounds from the given list that are less reactive than benzene towards electrophilic aromatic substitution is
questions.question:
Consider the following aromatic compounds:
Chlorobenzene, Anisole, Toluene, Nitrobenzene, Acetophenone, Phenol, Benzoic acid.

The number of compounds from the given list that are less reactive than benzene towards electrophilic aromatic substitution is
questions.solution:
Compounds that are less reactive than benzene towards electrophilic aromatic substitution are those that have deactivating groups attached to the benzene ring.

Let us evaluate the substituent in each compound:
1. Chlorobenzene: The $-\text{Cl}$ group is deactivating due to its strong $-I$ effect outweighing its $+R$ effect.
2. Anisole: The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group is activating ($+R > -I$).
3. Toluene: The $-\text{CH}_3$ group is activating (due to hyperconjugation and $+I$ effect).
4. Nitrobenzene: The $-\text{NO}_2$ group is strongly deactivating ($-R$ and $-I$).
5. Acetophenone: The $-\text{COCH}_3$ group is deactivating ($-R$ and $-I$).
6. Phenol: The $-\text{OH}$ group is activating ($+R > -I$).
7. Benzoic acid: The $-\text{COOH}$ group is deactivating ($-R$ and $-I$).

Therefore, the compounds less reactive than benzene are Chlorobenzene, Nitrobenzene, Acetophenone, and Benzoic acid. There are 4 such compounds.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A terminal alkyne $X$ undergoes partial reduction in the presence of $H_2$ and Lindlar's catalyst to form an alkene $Y$. When $Y$ is subjected to reductive ozonolysis, it produces a mixture of two aldehydes. If one of the aldehydes is formaldehyde and the other has a molar mass of $58 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, identify the starting alkyne $X$.
questions.question: A terminal alkyne $X$ undergoes partial reduction in the presence of $H_2$ and Lindlar's catalyst to form an alkene $Y$. When $Y$ is subjected to reductive ozonolysis, it produces a mixture of two aldehydes. If one of the aldehydes is formaldehyde and the other has a molar mass of $58 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, identify the starting alkyne $X$.
questions.solution:
The aldehyde with a molar mass of $58 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$ has the general formula $C_nH_{2n}O$.

$12n + 2n + 16 = 58$
$14n = 42 \Rightarrow n = 3$

Thus, the aldehyde is propanal ($CH_3CH_2CHO$).

The products of the reductive ozonolysis of alkene $Y$ are formaldehyde ($HCHO$) and propanal ($CH_3CH_2CHO$).

Reconstructing the alkene $Y$ by removing the oxygen atoms and joining the carbonyl carbons with a double bond gives but-1-ene ($CH_3CH_2CH=CH_2$).

Since $Y$ was formed by the partial reduction of a terminal alkyne $X$, the starting alkyne must be but-1-yne ($CH_3CH_2C \equiv CH$).

Answer: But-1-yne

questions.q:
Given below are two statements for the following reaction sequence:
Acetylene $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{CH}_3\text{I}]{\text{(i) } \text{NaNH}_2}$ P $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{CH}_3\text{I}]{\text{(i) } \text{NaNH}_2}$ Q
Q $\xrightarrow{\text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4, \text{Hg}^{2+}}$ S
Q $\xrightarrow{\text{Red hot Fe tube, } 873 \text{ K}}$ R

Statement I: Compound S gives a yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ but does not reduce Tollens' reagent.
Statement II: Compound R has 12 C-C sigma bonds and all its carbon atoms are $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Given below are two statements for the following reaction sequence:
Acetylene $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{CH}_3\text{I}]{\text{(i) } \text{NaNH}_2}$ P $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{CH}_3\text{I}]{\text{(i) } \text{NaNH}_2}$ Q
Q $\xrightarrow{\text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4, \text{Hg}^{2+}}$ S
Q $\xrightarrow{\text{Red hot Fe tube, } 873 \text{ K}}$ R

Statement I: Compound S gives a yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ but does not reduce Tollens' reagent.
Statement II: Compound R has 12 C-C sigma bonds and all its carbon atoms are $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.solution:
Acetylene reacts with 1 equivalent of $\text{NaNH}_2$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ to form propyne (P).
Propyne reacts with another equivalent of $\text{NaNH}_2$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ to form 2-butyne (Q).
Hydration of 2-butyne (Q) in the presence of dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{Hg}^{2+}$ yields 2-butanone (S).
2-Butanone is a methyl ketone, so it gives a positive iodoform test (yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$). Being a ketone, it does not reduce Tollens' reagent. Thus, Statement I is true.
Passing 2-butyne (Q) through a red-hot iron tube at 873 K causes cyclic polymerization to form hexamethylbenzene (R).
Hexamethylbenzene has 6 C-C sigma bonds in the benzene ring and 6 C-C sigma bonds connecting the methyl groups to the ring, making a total of 12 C-C sigma bonds. However, the 6 carbon atoms of the methyl groups are $\text{sp}^3$ hybridized. Thus, Statement II is false.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.q:
In a quantitative analysis, $0.3 \text{ g}$ of an organic compound was found to contain $60\%$ carbon by mass. Upon complete combustion, the mass of $\text{CO}_2$ gas produced from this sample is _______ $\text{mg}$.

[Given : Molar mass (in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$) $\text{C}: 12, \text{O}: 16$]
questions.question:
In a quantitative analysis, $0.3 \text{ g}$ of an organic compound was found to contain $60\%$ carbon by mass. Upon complete combustion, the mass of $\text{CO}_2$ gas produced from this sample is _______ $\text{mg}$.

[Given : Molar mass (in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$) $\text{C}: 12, \text{O}: 16$]
questions.solution:
Mass of carbon in the organic compound $= \dfrac{60}{100} \times 0.3 = 0.18 \text{ g}$

Applying the Principle of Atomic Conservation (POAC) on carbon:
Moles of carbon in compound $=$ Moles of $\text{CO}_2$ produced
$\dfrac{0.18}{12} = \dfrac{\text{Mass of CO}_2}{44}$

Mass of $\text{CO}_2 = \dfrac{0.18 \times 44}{12} = 0.66 \text{ g}$

Mass of $\text{CO}_2$ in mg $= 0.66 \times 1000 = 660 \text{ mg}$

Answer: $660$

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the mechanism of the nitration of benzene:

A. In the nitrating mixture, $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ acts as a Bronsted base.
B. The generation of the $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$ electrophile involves the heterolytic cleavage of the $\mathrm{O-N}$ bond in protonated nitric acid.
C. The intermediate arenium ion (sigma complex) formed during the attack of $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$ is aromatic in nature.
D. The breaking of the $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond to restore aromaticity is the rate-determining step.

Choose the correct statements from the options given below:
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the mechanism of the nitration of benzene:

A. In the nitrating mixture, $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ acts as a Bronsted base.
B. The generation of the $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$ electrophile involves the heterolytic cleavage of the $\mathrm{O-N}$ bond in protonated nitric acid.
C. The intermediate arenium ion (sigma complex) formed during the attack of $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$ is aromatic in nature.
D. The breaking of the $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond to restore aromaticity is the rate-determining step.

Choose the correct statements from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: In the nitrating mixture (concentrated $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ and concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$), $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ is a stronger acid and donates a proton to $\mathrm{HNO_3}$. Thus, $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ accepts a proton and acts as a Bronsted base.

Statement B is correct: The protonated nitric acid ($\mathrm{H_2O^+-NO_2}$) undergoes heterolytic cleavage of the $\mathrm{O-N}$ bond. The bonding electrons move to the more electronegative oxygen atom, releasing a neutral water molecule and generating the nitronium ion ($\mathrm{NO_2^+}$).

Statement C is incorrect: The intermediate arenium ion (sigma complex) has one $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybridized carbon atom, which breaks the continuous cyclic delocalization of $\pi$ electrons. Hence, it is non-aromatic.

Statement D is incorrect: In the electrophilic aromatic substitution of benzene, the formation of the arenium ion (attack of the electrophile on the benzene ring) is the slow, rate-determining step. The subsequent breaking of the $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond by a base to restore aromaticity is a fast step.

Answer: A and B only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aromatic, oxygen-containing compound 'X' gives a characteristic violet colour with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ solution. When 'X' is heated with zinc dust, it forms a hydrocarbon 'Y'. Compound 'Y' on treatment with oleum gives 'Z'. Compound 'Z' on fusion with $\text{NaOH}$ at high temperature followed by acidification regenerates 'X'. Identify the compounds 'Y' and 'Z' respectively.
questions.question: An aromatic, oxygen-containing compound 'X' gives a characteristic violet colour with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ solution. When 'X' is heated with zinc dust, it forms a hydrocarbon 'Y'. Compound 'Y' on treatment with oleum gives 'Z'. Compound 'Z' on fusion with $\text{NaOH}$ at high temperature followed by acidification regenerates 'X'. Identify the compounds 'Y' and 'Z' respectively.
questions.solution:
The characteristic violet colour with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ solution indicates that compound 'X' is a phenol.

Heating phenol (X) with zinc dust causes its reduction to benzene (compound 'Y').

Benzene undergoes sulfonation when treated with oleum (fuming sulfuric acid) to form benzenesulfonic acid (compound 'Z').

Fusion of benzenesulfonic acid with $\text{NaOH}$ followed by acidification replaces the $-\text{SO}_3\text{H}$ group with an $-\text{OH}$ group, regenerating phenol (X). Thus, Y is benzene and Z is benzenesulfonic acid.

Answer: Benzene and benzenesulfonic acid

questions.q:
Propyne is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:
(i) $\text{NaNH}_2$
(ii) $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$
(iii) $\text{Na}$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$
(iv) $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CCl}_4$

The final major product obtained is:
questions.question:
Propyne is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:
(i) $\text{NaNH}_2$
(ii) $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$
(iii) $\text{Na}$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$
(iv) $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CCl}_4$

The final major product obtained is:
questions.solution:
Steps (i) & (ii): Propyne reacts with $\text{NaNH}_2$ to form a propynide ion, which then acts as a nucleophile to attack $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ via an $S_N2$ mechanism, yielding 2-butyne.

Step (iii): Birch reduction of 2-butyne using $\text{Na}$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ stereoselectively produces trans-2-butene.

Step (iv): The addition of $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CCl}_4$ to an alkene proceeds via an anti-addition mechanism. The anti-addition of halogens to a symmetrical trans-alkene yields a meso compound (meso-2,3-dibromobutane).

Answer: A meso compound

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An alkyne $X$ with the molecular formula $C_5H_8$ does not yield a white precipitate when treated with ammoniacal $AgNO_3$ solution. $X$ is reduced with $Na$ in liquid $NH_3$ to give an alkene $Y$. $Y$ is then subjected to reductive ozonolysis ($O_3$ followed by $Zn/H_2O$) to yield a mixture of two carbonyl compounds. The sum of the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens in these two carbonyl compounds is:
questions.question: An alkyne $X$ with the molecular formula $C_5H_8$ does not yield a white precipitate when treated with ammoniacal $AgNO_3$ solution. $X$ is reduced with $Na$ in liquid $NH_3$ to give an alkene $Y$. $Y$ is then subjected to reductive ozonolysis ($O_3$ followed by $Zn/H_2O$) to yield a mixture of two carbonyl compounds. The sum of the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens in these two carbonyl compounds is:
questions.solution:
The molecular formula of $X$ is $C_5H_8$, which corresponds to an alkyne. Since it does not give a white precipitate with ammoniacal $AgNO_3$ (Tollens' reagent), it is an internal alkyne, not a terminal one.

The only internal alkyne with the formula $C_5H_8$ is pent-2-yne ($CH_3-C \equiv C-CH_2-CH_3$).

Reduction of pent-2-yne with $Na$ in liquid $NH_3$ (Birch reduction) yields trans-pent-2-ene ($Y$).

Reductive ozonolysis of pent-2-ene cleaves the double bond to form ethanal ($CH_3CHO$) and propanal ($CH_3CH_2CHO$).

In ethanal ($CH_3CHO$), there are $3\alpha$-hydrogens.
In propanal ($CH_3CH_2CHO$), there are $2\alpha$-hydrogens.

The total number of $\alpha$-hydrogens in the products is $3 + 2 = 5$.

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aromatic compound $X$ undergoes Birch reduction using sodium in liquid ammonia and ethanol to produce 1-methoxy-4-methylcyclohexa-1,4-diene as the major product. The IUPAC name of the reactant $X$ is:
questions.question: An aromatic compound $X$ undergoes Birch reduction using sodium in liquid ammonia and ethanol to produce 1-methoxy-4-methylcyclohexa-1,4-diene as the major product. The IUPAC name of the reactant $X$ is:
questions.solution:
In Birch reduction, electron-donating groups (EDGs) like $-\text{OCH}_3$ and $-\text{CH}_3$ direct the reduction such that the carbons bearing these groups remain $sp^2$ hybridized (i.e., they remain part of the double bonds).

The product is given as 1-methoxy-4-methylcyclohexa-1,4-diene. In this structure, both the methoxy group at C1 and the methyl group at C4 are attached to $sp^2$ hybridized carbons.

For both EDGs to remain on the double bonds of an isolated 1,4-diene system, they must be positioned para (1,4) to each other on the original benzene ring. Therefore, the starting aromatic compound $X$ must be 4-methoxytoluene.

Answer: 4-Methoxytoluene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Three structural isomers A, B, and C of an alkane with the molecular formula $C_5H_{12}$ undergo photochemical monochlorination. It is observed that isomer A yields 1, isomer B yields 3, and isomer C yields 4 structurally isomeric monochloro products. The correct increasing order of the melting points of these isomers is :
questions.question: Three structural isomers A, B, and C of an alkane with the molecular formula $C_5H_{12}$ undergo photochemical monochlorination. It is observed that isomer A yields 1, isomer B yields 3, and isomer C yields 4 structurally isomeric monochloro products. The correct increasing order of the melting points of these isomers is :
questions.solution:
The alkane $C_5H_{12}$ has three structural isomers: n-pentane, isopentane, and neopentane.

Based on the number of structurally isomeric monochloro products formed:
Neopentane has all 12 equivalent hydrogens, yielding 1 product. Thus, A is neopentane.
n-pentane has 3 sets of equivalent hydrogens, yielding 3 products. Thus, B is n-pentane.
Isopentane has 4 sets of equivalent hydrogens, yielding 4 products. Thus, C is isopentane.

The melting point of alkanes depends on how well the molecules pack in the solid crystal lattice. Neopentane (A) has a highly symmetrical, spherical structure, leading to the most efficient packing and the highest melting point.
Between n-pentane (B) and isopentane (C), isopentane is less symmetrical and packs less efficiently than the straight-chain n-pentane, resulting in the lowest melting point.

Therefore, the increasing order of their melting points is isopentane < n-pentane < neopentane, which corresponds to C < B < A.

Answer: C < B < A

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : In the chlorination of benzene, anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ acts as a Lewis acid to facilitate the generation of the electrophile $\mathrm{Cl^+}$.
Statement II : The Lewis acid promotes the reaction by donating a lone pair of electrons to the benzene ring to increase its nucleophilicity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : In the chlorination of benzene, anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ acts as a Lewis acid to facilitate the generation of the electrophile $\mathrm{Cl^+}$.
Statement II : The Lewis acid promotes the reaction by donating a lone pair of electrons to the benzene ring to increase its nucleophilicity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.solution:
In the chlorination of benzene, anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ acts as a Lewis acid. It accepts a lone pair of electrons from the chlorine molecule, polarizing the $\mathrm{Cl-Cl}$ bond and facilitating the generation of the electrophile (which can be considered as $\mathrm{Cl^+}$ or a highly polarized complex). Thus, Statement I is correct.

A Lewis acid is an electron-pair acceptor, not an electron-pair donor. It does not donate electrons to the benzene ring; rather, the benzene ring acts as a nucleophile and attacks the generated electrophile. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following aromatic compounds:
(I) Anisole
(II) Toluene
(III) Benzene
(IV) Chlorobenzene

The correct decreasing order of their reactivity towards electrophilic aromatic substitution is:
questions.question:
Consider the following aromatic compounds:
(I) Anisole
(II) Toluene
(III) Benzene
(IV) Chlorobenzene

The correct decreasing order of their reactivity towards electrophilic aromatic substitution is:
questions.solution:
The reactivity of an aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution depends on the electron density on the ring. Electron-donating groups increase reactivity, while electron-withdrawing groups decrease it.

In Anisole (I), the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group is strongly activating due to its strong $+M$ (resonance) effect.
In Toluene (II), the $-\text{CH}_3$ group is weakly activating due to hyperconjugation and $+I$ effect.
Benzene (III) is the standard reference.
In Chlorobenzene (IV), the $-\text{Cl}$ atom is deactivating because its electron-withdrawing inductive effect ($-I$) outweighs its electron-donating resonance effect ($+M$).

Therefore, the decreasing order of reactivity is Anisole > Toluene > Benzene > Chlorobenzene, which corresponds to I > II > III > IV.

Answer: I > II > III > IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following cycloalkenes, upon reductive ozonolysis, yields a product that gives both a positive iodoform test and a positive Tollens' test?
questions.question: Which of the following cycloalkenes, upon reductive ozonolysis, yields a product that gives both a positive iodoform test and a positive Tollens' test?
questions.solution:
To give a positive Tollens' test, the product must contain an aldehyde group ($-CHO$). To give a positive iodoform test, the product must contain a methyl ketone group ($-COCH_3$).

Let us evaluate the reductive ozonolysis product for each option:

1-methylcyclohexene undergoes reductive ozonolysis to yield 6-oxoheptanal ($CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CHO$). This molecule contains both a methyl ketone and an aldehyde group, so it will give both tests positive.

1,2-dimethylcyclohexene yields octane-2,7-dione ($CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CO-CH_3$). It lacks an aldehyde group, so it gives a negative Tollens' test.

3-methylcyclohexene yields 2-methylhexanedial ($OHC-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CHO$). It lacks a methyl ketone group, so it gives a negative iodoform test.

1-phenylcyclohexene yields 6-phenyl-6-oxohexanal ($Ph-CO-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CHO$). It contains a phenyl ketone (not a methyl ketone) and an aldehyde, so it gives a negative iodoform test.

Therefore, 1-methylcyclohexene is the correct answer.

Answer: 1-methylcyclohexene
